assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and its translation into incretin-based drugs is one of the most consequential medical advances of recent decades, linking basic gut-hormone biology to transformative treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity with documented cardiovascular and wider benefits. The chain from discovery to patients is unusually clear and the impact is already global.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology of proglucagon-derived peptides and GLP-1 action) and Drucker (GLP-1 biology, receptor signalling and therapeutic concept) are the strongest scientific anchors; Knudsen led the development of long-acting analogues (liraglutide, semaglutide) that made the therapy practical. Mojsov's early peptide characterisation is also credited and her share is contested; a three-person configuration necessarily leaves out a legitimate claimant.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple independent large clinical trials, regulatory approvals and real-world use over many years. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation among Mojsov, Habener-type contributions to proglucagon biology, and pharmaceutical development is disputed; I rely on memory of the priority literature and have not verified it.
Whether the committee wishes to honour a drug-development contribution alongside basic physiology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a new mode of intracellular communication from the endoplasmic reticulum to the nucleus and a general logic of proteostasis, with deep consequences for secretory physiology, metabolism, neurodegeneration and cancer. The concept is original, clear and widely taught.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori are the natural pair: Mori identified the signalling pathway components in yeast and mammals and Walter elucidated the Ire1 mechanism, unconventional splicing and the integrated stress response connection. Cleanly bounded two-person credit; others (e.g. Ron, Kaufman, Shen) contributed to downstream branches.
assessment.maturity: Mature: confirmed across yeast, mammals and disease models for over two decades, with the mechanism well understood at molecular level.
uncertainties: Direct clinical impact is still emerging (e.g. ISRIB-type modulators), so the medical dimension is less established than the basic one.
The relative weight of PERK/ATF6 branch discoverers is something I cannot fully resolve.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered CAR-T cells created a new class of living drugs and produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukaemias and lymphomas, with clear clinical and conceptual impact on cancer immunotherapy and cell engineering.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain led the translational design and clinical proof of second-generation CARs (costimulatory domains) in CD19 therapy. Rosenberg contributed adoptive cell transfer and early clinical CAR and TIL work, but the supplied credit omits early CAR-concept originators such as Eshhar, so the configuration is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature: approved products, long follow-up in leukaemia and lymphoma. Some limits remain in solid tumours and toxicity, but the core discovery is stable.
uncertainties: Missing originators in the credited list complicate fair allocation.
Rosenberg's role versus June and Sadelain is a judgment call; I did not verify details independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics transformed how neural circuits, including the motor and spinal circuits I study, are dissected causally, and has spread across all of biology; the channelrhodopsin discovery and its demonstration as a neuronal tool are original and enormously enabling. Impact on basic science is exceptional, though therapeutic application is just beginning.
assessment.attribution: Credit is crowded: Nagel and Hegemann (channelrhodopsin identification and characterisation, with Bamberg), Boyden and Deisseroth (neuronal deployment), Miesenböck (earlier genetic photostimulation). I would favour Deisseroth with Nagel and Hegemann, but this excludes Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck, a real cost to fairness.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a method with extensive independent use for two decades; clinical translation (e.g. retinal optogenetics) is early.
uncertainties: Attribution among six credited people is hard to reduce to three.
It is a tool rather than a disease mechanism; the committee may weigh this differently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 revealed that cell survival rather than proliferation drives some cancers and defined the regulation of apoptosis, culminating in BH3-mimetic therapy (venetoclax) for leukaemia. A coherent arc from basic discovery to approved targeted therapy.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams cloned and characterised the BCL-2 family and its translocation context, and Vaux showed its anti-death function. Strasser extended the family biology. Tsujimoto and Korsmeyer are not in the credited list, so the configuration may be incomplete; I would propose Cory, Adams and Vaux.
assessment.maturity: Mature; clinical validation through venetoclax in CLL and other malignancies is established.
uncertainties: Priority issues with contributors outside the supplied credit names.
Whether apoptosis has been recognised enough already (2002 prize) to reduce urgency.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway defined how cytosolic DNA is sensed and triggers innate immunity, interferon responses, autoimmunity and anti-tumour immunity, a unifying concept in infection, inflammation and cancer biology.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the second messenger cGAMP; Barber identified STING as the adaptor. These are the two decisive discoveries; other credited names (Ishikawa, Sun, Wu) contributed but are less likely to be core to a prize.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature; the mechanism is robust and widely replicated, but clinical translation (STING agonists, inhibitors) has been slow, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Ishikawa's early STING contribution relative to Barber could be raised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Chaperonin-assisted folding established that proteins can fold with active help in cellular compartments, a foundational concept in protein biology with consequences for aggregation diseases and proteostasis.
assessment.attribution: Hartl and Horwich jointly defined the GroEL/GroES-type mechanism and its mitochondrial role in a clean two-person credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely confirmed, with structural and mechanistic detail; the work is decades old, so recognition is not premature, but disease relevance is indirect.
uncertainties: The impact is largely conceptual and the field may have been implicitly covered by other proteostasis recognition.
Contribution of Ellis and others to the chaperone concept lies outside the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Adult stem-cell-derived organoids created a reproducible culture system for studying epithelial tissue renewal and disease, now used widely in disease modelling, drug testing and personalised medicine.
assessment.attribution: Clevers led the Lgr5 stem-cell discovery and organoid culture, with Sato as the first author of the key culture work; the two-person configuration is clear, though Clevers is likely the principal figure.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature as a platform, with broad independent uptake; clinical impact (e.g. predictive use in cystic fibrosis) is still developing.
uncertainties: Whether Sato's share would be deemed sufficient for a prize.
Translational medical impact not yet fully demonstrated.
